title: Installation Jobs Crew Planning Standard: Crew Days Planned
content:
**Crew planning standard — crew days for an Installation Jobs booking**

When a crew date is booked on an **Installation Jobs** record, the crew days planned are the units the crew plans for, which are the job's units (openings, or door units for a door job), divided by the crew's daily pace, rounded up to a whole day. The crew's daily pace is the method's openings per crew day, shown in the product's method schedule, and it never falls below 1 opening a day.

The crew days planned are always a whole number of days: any fraction of a day left by the division counts as a full day.

## Elements of the plan

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Units the crew plans for | the job's units: the openings or door units recorded on the job |
| Daily pace | the method's openings per crew day, never below 1 opening a day |
| Crew days planned | the units the crew plans for divided by the daily pace, rounded up to a whole day |

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

| Units the crew plans for | Daily pace | Units divided by pace | Crew days planned |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 8 | 2 | 2 |
| 17 | 8 | 2.125 | 3 |
| 9 | 4 | 2.25 | 3 |
| 3 | 1 | 3 | 3 |

## Points of the standard

- **Rounding.** The rounding is always upward to the next whole day; a plan never rounds down.
- **Which method.** The pace is the one for the installation method named on the job.
